download.title: 6 Jars Finance — Six Jars Budgeting App
download.metaDescription: Allocate your salary between everyday spending, savings, and financial goals before you start spending.

hero.title: Stay in control of today’s spending and feel confident about tomorrow
hero.lead: 6 Jars Finance helps you divide your salary in advance, so you know how much you can spend on cafes and entertainment, set money aside for a vacation or a major purchase, and gradually build an emergency fund.
hero.screenshotAlt: 6 Jars Finance home screen showing six jars and their balances

benefits.title: Know how much you can spend
benefits.text: You can see separate amounts for everyday expenses, cafes, entertainment, and other categories. There is no need to keep checking your total balance and wondering whether you can afford a purchase.

benefits.title: Save before you spend
benefits.text: You can immediately set aside part of your salary for a vacation, a major purchase, or another goal. This money stays separate from everyday spending instead of quietly disappearing by the end of the month.

benefits.title: Build an emergency fund over time
benefits.text: By regularly setting aside even a small part of your salary, you can build an emergency fund for illness, broken appliances, delayed salary payments, and other unexpected situations.

about.title: Built from personal experience
paragraphs: My name is Artem D. I have worked as a professional software developer since 2017 and created 6 Jars Finance.

I have used the Six Jars budgeting method for more than 10 years. Thanks to it, I do not have to keep wondering whether I can afford a new board game or go to a cafe, whether I will have enough money for a vacation, or whether I will be able to pay the rent on time if my paycheck is delayed.

Over the years, I tried several apps based on the Six Jars method. What frustrated me most was that the number of jars was always strictly limited to six. There was no way to add a seventh jar or remove one I did not need.

That is why I created 6 Jars Finance, where you can adapt your jar system as your circumstances and financial priorities change. I use the app regularly myself, so I continue to add new features and make it easier to use.

items.question: Do I have to follow the traditional Six Jars allocation exactly?
items.answer: No. The traditional allocation is a ready-made starting point, not a fixed set of rules.

items.question: Can I customize the app to suit my needs?
items.answer: Yes. You can rename the six default jars, remove jars you do not need, and choose different percentages. You can also create additional jars if needed.

items.question: Do I need to record every purchase separately?
items.answer: No. You can combine several purchases from the same jar into a single entry. For example, you do not have to record every supermarket purchase separately—you can simply enter the total amount spent on groceries.

items.question: What if I cannot afford to save right now?
items.answer: You decide how much money to put toward savings. You can start with a small amount or, for now, allocate your entire salary to current expenses—the app does not require you to save a fixed percentage.

items.question: How is this different from a regular expense tracker?
items.answer: Regular expense trackers mainly help you record purchases and see where your money has already gone. 6 Jars Finance automatically divides your salary between the spending and saving categories you set up in advance, so you can always see how much is available in each jar without dipping into money set aside for a vacation, a major purchase, or another goal.

guide.title: Want to understand the method in more detail?
guide.text: If you are unsure whether the Six Jars method will work for you or do not fully understand how it works, read the detailed guide. In it, I use practical examples and my own experience to explain how to apply the method in real life.

privacy.metaDescription: Privacy Policy for the application A.D.A - Artem D.

general.title: 1. General Provisions
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy describes how data is processed when using the mobile application. The app is designed with local data storage in mind (offline-first). Financial records and other user-created app data are stored locally on the user's device and are not transferred to the developer.
The app may use third-party services for technical purposes, such as crash and error reporting. These services may process technical diagnostic data needed to detect, diagnose, and fix errors.

userData.title: 2.1 Data entered by the user
userData.intro: The user enters the following into the app:
items: jar names, account names, notes, and other user settings
userData.outro: This data is stored locally on the user's device, is not transferred to the developer, is not copied to the developer's servers, and is not shared with third parties. The developer has no technical ability to access this data.

platformData.title: 2.2 Platform technical data
paragraphs: When installing and using the app, the Google Play platform may automatically process technical data such as device information, operating system version, diagnostic data, and crash reports.
Such data is processed by Google services in accordance with their own privacy policy. The developer does not receive the user's personal data from Google.

purchases.title: 2.3 In-app purchases
paragraphs: The app may use in-app purchases processed through Google Play. Payment processing is handled by Google's infrastructure. The developer does not receive bank card data, does not store payment information, and does not have access to the user's financial details.

crashes.title: 2.4 Crash and error reporting
paragraphs: The app uses Sentry, a third-party error monitoring service, to process crash reports and technical diagnostic data on behalf of the developer.

When an error occurs, the app may send technical diagnostic information to Sentry, such as crash logs, stack traces, app version, operating system version, device model, and other technical details related to the error.

Sentry is configured with default personal data collection disabled. The app does not intentionally send financial records, transaction data, jar names, tags, notes, account names, or other user-created financial content to Sentry.
The developer uses error reports only to improve app stability, diagnose technical issues, and fix bugs.
Because the app does not use accounts or assign user identifiers for error reporting, the developer may not be able to identify and delete a specific user's error reports.

storage.title: 3. Data storage
paragraphs: Financial records and other user-created app data are stored locally on the user's device in the app's database. Deleting the app results in deletion of locally stored data unless the user has created a backup beforehand. The developer does not store copies of this user-created app data and has no access to it.
Technical crash and diagnostic data may be processed by Sentry for error monitoring purposes.

thirdParties.title: 4. Transfer of data to third parties
paragraphs: The developer does not sell user data and does not transfer user-created financial data to third parties.
Financial records, transactions, tags, jar names, notes, settings, and backups are not transferred to the developer or to external servers by the app.
Technical crash and diagnostic data may be processed by Sentry on behalf of the developer for the purpose of detecting, diagnosing, and fixing errors.

backups.title: 5. Backups
paragraphs: If the app provides the ability to create a backup, the backup file is created by the user and saved at their discretion. The developer does not have access to backups.

rights.title: 6. User rights
items: delete locally stored app data by deleting the app or clearing the app data in device settings
opt out of using in-app purchases
rights.outro: Because the app does not use accounts or assign user identifiers for error reporting, the developer may not be able to identify and delete a specific user's error reports.

security.title: 7. Security
paragraphs: The app does not transmit the user's financial data over the internet. Technical crash and diagnostic data, if sent, is transmitted through a secure connection.
The user is responsible for the security of their device and any backups created.

changes.title: 8. Policy changes
paragraphs: An updated version of the policy is published on the app's official page.
